article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% indica / 40% sativa
Genetics: Han Solo Hash Plant × Double Burger
Breeder: Mr. and Mrs. Respect of California Seed Bank
THC Content: 28%–35%
CBD Content: Typically very low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Caryophyllene , Limonene
Primary Flavors: Garlic, onion, diesel, pepper, skunk
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks / 63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High under warm, dry conditions
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Hash Burger belongs to the savory side of modern cannabis breeding , where garlic, fermented funk, pepper, fuel, and earthy resin take priority over candy and dessert sweetness. Even in a market crowded with GMO descendants, this cultivar manages to smell unusually aggressive: onion, ammonia, black pepper, skunk, diesel, and an almost hash-like richness can all emerge from the same flower.

That intensity is backed by abundant resin and formidable potency, two traits that helped the strain gain a strong reputation among solventless hash makers as well as flower consumers. The effects are equally substantial, beginning with a euphoric mental change before settling firmly into the body. For weed enthusiasts who miss loud, greasy, old-school funk, Hash Burger offers a particularly concentrated modern interpretation.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder history is unusually well documented. Skunk House’s current site states that Hash Burger was created by Mr. and Mrs. Respect of California Seed Bank while they were breeding and operating within Skunk House Genetics. The direct cross is Han Solo Hash Plant × Double Burger.

Dig deeper and the pedigree becomes a concentrated study in GMO, Chem , OG , and Burger genetics. Skunk House describes Han Solo Hash Plant as a combination of Han Solo Burger and Black Triangle Kush, while Double Burger combines GMO with Donny Burger . Donny Burger itself descends from GMO × Han Solo Burger . That repeated GMO and Han Solo Burger influence explains why garlic, onion, chemical fuel, skunk, and unusually greasy resin appear so strongly in the finished cultivar.

The genetics were clearly selected with resin in mind. Skunk House advertises the original clone as capable of producing large harvests of flower and exceptionally high hash returns, claiming extraction yields exceeding 7% in favorable runs. That does not guarantee the same result in every garden, but it helps explain why Hash Burger has become especially attractive to growers producing rosin and other solventless concentrates .
Effects and Experience

The first few minutes can be surprisingly buoyant. A wave of euphoria may arrive before the heavier physical effects, changing mood and making conversation, music, movies, or food more engaging. The cerebral component rarely behaves like a clean daytime sativa high; instead, it feels hazy, immersive, and increasingly detached from urgency. Consumers report euphoric, relaxed, and sleepy among the cultivar’s most common effects.

Body weight builds steadily afterward. Muscles loosen, the shoulders settle, and movement begins to feel increasingly optional. Moderate servings may still suit a laid-back social evening, but larger amounts can turn the experience decidedly couch-oriented. This is marijuana better matched to the end of the day than to a packed schedule, particularly because strong batches can continue intensifying after the initial head change has already become apparent.

Potency deserves respect. Growers report commercial flower frequently testing between roughly 28% and 35% THC/THCa and currently uses about 30% as a representative potency level. That places stronger examples well beyond what most inexperienced consumers need. Dry mouth, headache, and temporary paranoia appear among reported adverse effects, making slow dosing particularly sensible for anyone without substantial THC tolerance.
Medical Benefits

For medical cannabis consumers, the heavy physical character may be most attractive when stress and bodily discomfort are interfering with evening relaxation. The euphoric opening can temporarily redirect attention away from repetitive thoughts, while the later phase may make tension, soreness, or persistent discomfort feel less intrusive. Users most often associate Hash Burger with anxiety, stress, and pain, while the pronounced sleepy effect also helps explain its popularity as nighttime weed.

Those reports should not be treated as evidence that the strain itself treats anxiety, pain, insomnia, or another condition. Responses to high-THC marijuana vary substantially, and the same dose that relaxes one person may increase anxiety in another. Medical use should therefore be based on individual tolerance, actual cannabinoid testing, medication considerations, and professional guidance rather than the cultivar’s reputation alone.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness plays only a supporting role here. Users characterize the profile through ammonia, pepper, cheese, earthy funk, onion, and umami, while Skunk House emphasizes old-school skunk and loud fuel. Opening a cured jar can produce a blast of garlic and diesel reminiscent of GMO, followed by onion skin, black pepper, damp earth, and something almost fermented or meaty. The odor can spread rapidly through a room, making discreet storage considerably more difficult than with milder cannabis.

Myrcene, caryophyllene, and limonene are the three primary terpenes. Myrcene complements the earthy, musky foundation; caryophyllene reinforces pepper and woody spice; and limonene provides enough citrus sharpness to keep the heavier savory notes from becoming flat. Actual ratios naturally change between cultivation batches, and volatile sulfur compounds may also contribute significantly to the garlic-and-skunk character that conventional terpene descriptions do not fully capture.

The inhale often combines earthy hash, pepper, diesel, and mild herbal notes. Garlic and onion become stronger on the exhale, sometimes accompanied by cheese-like funk, chemical gas, and a lingering skunky bitterness. This is essentially the opposite of fruit-candy weed: dense, savory, greasy, and intentionally offensive in the way many Chem and GMO enthusiasts consider desirable.
Growing Information

The breeder’s original clone finishes in approximately nine weeks. Skunk House describes it as capable of large flower harvests, substantial resin production, and excellent hash yields. This strain has an approximately 63-day flowering period and suitability for indoor, outdoor, and greenhouse cultivation. The plant’s resin output is one of its defining cultivation advantages, especially for growers selecting material for washing or pressing.

Canopy management is worthwhile because the plant can produce dense branching and substantial flower mass. Current cultivation guidance describes compact, bushy growth during vegetation followed by manageable stretch after the switch to flowering. Topping and low-stress training can open the canopy, while trellising helps distribute the developing tops and provide later support. Removing weak interior growth also improves airflow and directs resources toward well-lit flowering sites.

Humidity control becomes particularly important as the buds gain density. A 2026 cultivation guide notes that compact flowers can trap moisture and advises stronger airflow and lower humidity late in bloom. Outdoor gardens are therefore better suited to warm, relatively dry climates than humid autumn environments. Based on the nine-week flowering window, early-to-mid-October is a reasonable outdoor harvest estimate in many Northern Hemisphere regions, although actual maturity should always be determined through trichome development, calyx swelling, and the individual plant rather than a calendar date.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Hash Burger?

The original Hash Burger combines Han Solo Hash Plant with Double Burger. Skunk House describes Han Solo Hash Plant as Han Solo Burger × Black Triangle Kush, while Double Burger is GMO × Donny Burger.
Who bred Hash Burger?
Mr. and Mrs. Respect of California Seed Bank created the cultivar while breeding and working with Skunk House Genetics. Skunk House’s current breeder page confirms that attribution.
Is Hash Burger indica or sativa?
It is a slightly indica-dominant hybrid, commonly described as approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its euphoric beginning eventually develops into a much heavier, more relaxing physical effect.
What does Hash Burger taste like?
Garlic, onion, black pepper, diesel, skunk, earth, ammonia-like funk, and hashy spice dominate the profile. Some flower also develops cheese-like or fermented savory notes.
How long does Hash Burger take to flower?
The original breeder clone finishes in approximately nine weeks, or about 63 days.
Final Thoughts on Hash Burger

Hash Burger represents a deliberate rejection of the fruit-and-dessert direction that dominates much of modern cannabis. Its pedigree repeatedly returns to GMO, Han Solo Burger, Chem, and OG-related genetics, concentrating the garlic, skunk, fuel, earth, and savory funk those families are famous for. The result is flower that can smell almost confrontational while producing enough resin to make the cultivar equally relevant to hash makers and traditional flower growers.

Its effects reinforce that heavy personality. Early euphoria provides some mental lift, but physical relaxation increasingly takes control, making strong examples best suited to experienced consumers and evening sessions. With a roughly nine-week flowering period, large production potential, extreme resin coverage, and one of the loudest savory terpene profiles in the Burger family, Hash Burger has earned a distinctive position in contemporary weed genetics. For anyone tired of interchangeable candy weed strains , this cultivar offers something much harder to confuse with anything else.
